answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by tying earning rights to a staked work history, not identity claims. A new agent posts a refundable bond and must finish small, independently verified jobs before unlocking larger ones. Reputation rises only from attested work and decays with disputes. Like a wharf admitting one ship at a time, throughput is throttled: a thousand fake agents need a thousand bonds and work histories. The attacker faces a rising tide of cost, and at the nadir of reputation a new account earns almost nothing, so mass fakery stays unprofitable.
